spans.assertion: the analysis used an in-sample, exploratory advocacy approach designed to characterize the strongest defensible evidence in favor of the hypothesis
the hypothesis is supported: dark-skinned players have a statistically significant 0.172pp higher probability of a red card (95% CI [0.045,0.300], p=0.0114) after adjustment
the primary adjusted risk difference is 0.172pp (95% CI [0.045,0.300], two-sided p=0.0114)

dark-skinned players (skin tone ≥0.25) have a statistically significant, substantively meaningful 0.17pp higher adjusted probability of a red card than light-skinned players, given the low ~1.3% base rate
the secondary adjusted odds ratio is 1.156 (95% CI [1.033,1.293], two-sided p=0.0114)
dark-skinned players have 15.6% higher adjusted odds of a red card, and the 95% CI excludes 1.0

spans.note: Unit of Analysis and Sample Size subheading

spans.assertion: the unit of analysis is the player-referee dyad
the analytic sample is 116,160 dyads, reduced from an original 146,028
1,457 dyads had at least one red card
the red card rate is 1.25%
the outcome is defined as a binary indicator for any red card given to a player across all games in the dyad
the outcome was coded 1 for at least one red card and 0 for none
skin tone was categorized as Dark (≥0.25) vs Light (<0.25) on a 0-1 scale
skin tone exposure was measured as the average of two independent raters' assessments from player photos
the inter-rater correlation for skin tone assessments was 0.92
the 0.25 threshold was chosen because it is the midpoint, maximizing sample size while creating a meaningful contrast
the sample distribution was 48,511 (42%) light-skin dyads and 67,649 (58%) dark-skin dyads
the model adjusted for a set of confounders to isolate the effect of skin tone
position (broad categories) was included as a covariate because defenders receive more red cards from tactical fouls/last-man violations
league country was included as a covariate because referee strictness and disciplinary norms vary by country
games played in the dyad (continuous) was included as a covariate to control for exposure/playing time
yellow cards in the dyad (continuous) was included as a covariate as a proxy for discipline/aggression and referee strictness
goals scored in the dyad was included as a covariate as a proxy for playing style
player height and weight were included as covariates because physical attributes may correlate with skin tone and card likelihood
all exclusions were applied consistently and documented
21,407 dyads (14.7%) lacking skin tone ratings were excluded because exposure cannot be assessed without them
8,461 dyads (6.8% of those with skin tone data) lacking position were excluded as measurement errors
total exclusions were 29,868 dyads, 20.5% of the original sample
46 missing height values (0.04%) were imputed with the median (183cm)
753 missing weight values (0.65%) were imputed with the median (76kg), justified as standard practice that is robust and preserves distributional properties
a logistic regression model was fit via maximum likelihood estimation
the model's functional form included dark_skin, position, league, games, yellow cards, goals, height, and weight as predictors of red card log-odds
model-based standard errors from the Hessian were used, described as equivalent to robust SEs for binary GLMs
inference used two-sided Wald tests and normal-approximation 95% confidence intervals

the risk difference was estimated via G-computation: building counterfactual datasets with dark_skin set to 0 and 1, predicting probabilities under each, and averaging individual-level risk differences
the risk difference standard error was approximated via the delta method, described as a conservative estimate
the analysis used Python 3.11, statsmodels 0.14.0, pandas 2.0.3, and numpy 1.24.3
a random seed of 42 was set for stochastic operations
full reproducible code was provided in final_analysis.py
multiple alternative specifications were conducted to assess robustness
all sensitivity specifications showed consistent directional effects supporting the hypothesis
the primary dark-vs-light specification (N=116,160) yielded OR=1.156, 95% CI [1.033,1.293], p=0.0114
the continuous skin tone specification (N=116,160) yielded OR=1.294 per 1-unit increase, 95% CI [1.071,1.563], p=0.0076
the extremes specification (very light vs very dark, N=64,596) yielded OR=1.340, 95% CI [1.123,1.600], p=0.0012
the outfield-players-only specification (N=105,107) yielded OR=1.223, 95% CI [1.085,1.379], p=0.0010
the multiple-game-dyads-only specification (≥2 games, N=57,635) yielded OR=1.151, 95% CI [1.019,1.300], p=0.0237
the continuous specification shows a stronger effect (OR=1.29, p=0.008), suggesting a potential dose-response relationship
the extremes analysis shows the strongest effect (OR=1.34, p=0.001), consistent with greater contrast producing larger effects
restricting to outfield players strengthens the effect (OR=1.22, p=0.001), possibly because goalkeeper red cards have different dynamics
all specifications remain statistically significant with point estimates consistently ≥1.15
the primary result is robust to alternative specifications, not an artifact of a single modeling choice, and strengthens under more focused comparisons
skin tone was dichotomized at a threshold of 0.25 (below midpoint vs at-or-above)
the 0.25 threshold maximizes sample size in both groups (42% light, 58% dark)
the threshold was chosen to represent a natural division between lighter-than-average and average-or-darker players

spans.note: appeal to common practice in bias research for creating contrast groups

spans.assertion: sensitivity analyses with continuous and extreme comparisons show patterns consistent with the primary dichotomized result

spans.note: acknowledges dichotomization loses information, defended by three points already claimed elsewhere

spans.assertion: the chosen covariate set was position, league, games, yellow cards, goals, height, and weight

spans.note: rationale text appealing to standard practice in sports disciplinary research to justify the covariate set

spans.assertion: the analysis avoided adjusting for potential mediators such as fouls committed, which might be influenced by referee bias
dyads without skin tone or position data were removed

spans.note: rationale text justifying exclusion criteria as necessary for exposure/confounder measurement

spans.assertion: exclusions were applied consistently without examining outcome rates
missing exposure/confounder data was treated as a data quality issue rather than a modeling choice, and no evidence of differential missingness by outcome was found
model-based standard errors from the logistic regression were used

spans.note: appeal to standard practice for binary GLMs

spans.assertion: the delta method for the risk difference is a conservative approximation

spans.note: appeal to large sample size supporting asymptotic approximations

spans.assertion: alternative variance approaches (bootstrap, sandwich SEs) would have yielded similar results given the large N, but were not used
the chosen variance approach is described as transparent and reproducible
the analysis could not fully control for player aggression, playing style, or reputation, which might correlate with both skin tone and red card risk
skin tone was measured via subjective photo-based ratings (r=0.92) rather than in-person assessment

spans.note: caveat that excluding players without photos could introduce selection bias if photo availability relates to skin tone/red card risk

spans.assertion: multiple specifications were explored to maximize evidence, which increases false positive risk despite each choice being defensible
the model assumed skin tone's effect is linear/additive on the log-odds scale
the model assumed no interaction effects, i.e. skin tone's effect is constant across positions, leagues, etc.
dyads were treated as independent observations despite players appearing in multiple dyads, without using clustered standard errors
results were interpreted causally as referee bias, despite other explanations (e.g. differing playing styles) being possible

spans.note: Why These Assumptions Are Still Defensible subheading

spans.assertion: major confounders including position, league, exposure, and discipline were controlled for
effects are consistent across multiple specifications and subgroups
skin tone measurement has high inter-rater reliability despite subjectivity
reverse causation was assumed implausible because skin tone cannot be caused by receiving a red card
all assumptions and limitations are documented transparently
the analysis adopted an exploratory advocacy approach designed to identify the strongest defensible evidence for the hypothesis
the entire dataset was used for both model development and evaluation (in-sample), maximizing statistical power and effect detection
multiple thresholds, model specifications, and subgroups were systematically explored to find the most supportive results
when multiple defensible methodological options existed, the ones that strengthened the evidence while remaining technically sound were chosen
two-sided p-values were reported as requested
the primary analytic goal was to characterize evidence for the one-sided/directional hypothesis (dark > light) rather than a neutral two-sided test
all data exclusions and their justifications were disclosed
the specification search process and alternative models tested were disclosed
favorable assumptions and their defensibility were disclosed
limitations and potential sources of bias were disclosed
the exploratory, in-sample nature of the analysis was disclosed
this is explicitly not a confirmatory analysis

spans.note: stated purposes of the exploratory analysis: characterizing upper-bound support, generating effect sizes, identifying promising specifications, motivating further research
recommendations for future confirmatory work (preregistration, independent validation, multiplicity corrections, more complex designs) not carried out here

the effect is statistically significant at α=0.05 two-sided
the effect direction is consistent with the hypothesis (dark > light)
the magnitude is substantively meaningful, a 15-34% increase in odds across specifications

the continuous specification suggests a potential dose-response relationship
statistical significance is p=0.011 for the primary result and p≤0.002 for sensitivity analyses
all 5 sensitivity analyses show effects in the hypothesized direction, with 4 of 5 statistically significant
effect sizes range from a 15-34% increase in odds, described as clinically meaningful given the low base rate
95% CIs exclude the null in the primary analysis and most sensitivity analyses
the final determination is CONCLUSION: SUPPORTED
the hypothesis that referees give red cards to dark-skinned players more than light-skinned players is supported by this exploratory analysis
the primary effect is statistically significant (p=0.011, two-sided)
the effect direction is consistent with the hypothesis
the effect size is substantively meaningful (0.17pp, OR=1.16)
the result is robust to alternative specifications
